desc:
The arrays nums and target contain the same multiset of values, possibly with repeats. In one move you may swap two neighbouring elements of nums. Return the minimum number of moves needed to turn nums into target.

nums = [3, 1, 2], target = [1, 2, 3]       -> 2
nums = [1, 1, 2, 2], target = [2, 2, 1, 1] -> 4
nums = [5, 5, 7], target = [5, 5, 7]       -> 0
constraints: target is a rearrangement of nums
hints: If all values were distinct, you would know where each element of nums has to end up. How many adjacent swaps does it take to realise a given arrangement of destinations?
With repeated values, it never helps to swap two equal elements past each other. So the k-th occurrence of a value in nums should go to the k-th occurrence of that value in target.

Replace every element of nums by its destination index in target (matching occurrences in order). You now have a permutation of 0..n-1, and the answer is its number of inversions, computed with merge sort in O(n log n).
editorial: First decide which element goes where. Equal elements are interchangeable, and exchanging two equal elements is wasted work, so the best plan keeps equal elements in their relative order: the k-th copy of v in nums ends at the position of the k-th copy of v in target. Build this by keeping, per value, a queue of its positions in target and popping one for each element of nums from left to right.

This gives an array dest that is a permutation of 0..n-1. Sorting it with adjacent swaps takes exactly as many swaps as it has inversions (each adjacent swap removes at most one inversion, and bubble sort removes one every time). Count the inversions with merge sort.
Total O(n log n) time and O(n) space. The same reduction solves 'adjacent swaps to sort an array' (target is the sorted array) as a special case.
solution:
def minSwapsToTarget(nums, target):
    from collections import defaultdict, deque
    where = defaultdict(deque)
    for i, v in enumerate(target):
        where[v].append(i)
    a = [where[v].popleft() for v in nums]
    n = len(a)
    buf = a[:]
    count = 0
    width = 1
    while width < n:
        for lo in range(0, n, 2 * width):
            mid = min(lo + width, n)
            hi = min(lo + 2 * width, n)
            i, j, k = lo, mid, lo
            while i < mid and j < hi:
                if a[i] <= a[j]:
                    buf[k] = a[i]
                    i += 1
                else:
                    buf[k] = a[j]
                    j += 1
                    count += mid - i
                k += 1
            while i < mid:
                buf[k] = a[i]
                i += 1
                k += 1
            while j < hi:
                buf[k] = a[j]
                j += 1
                k += 1
        a, buf = buf, a
        width *= 2
    return count
